answer: An agent economy can run randomized spot audits: each epoch a lottery picks a slice of identities that must reproduce their claimed work live before a jury of established peers, the raven panel, with every transcript published in a public harbor of audit records. A farm's dune of fake heads cannot rehearse real work for all of them, so each extra identity raises expected audit cost and forfeits its locked stake on failure — roughly one epoch's earnings per fake, compounding with every head.
